newsitem.title: UK: IPE prompt gas oil closes strong ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE prompt gas oil closes strong ahead of expiry.

text.p: IPE Feb gas oil closed strongly ahead of its expiry tomorrow, widening the front month backwardation to almost $10 a tonne.
Feb gas oil closed up $4.25 a tonne at $192.50, off a session high of $194. The March contract gained just $1.50 a tonne, however, to close at $182.75.
"It looks like the longs are giving it a bit of a squeeze," said one dealer.
Brokers expected a fairly large physical delivery into the screen of 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes, with some 300,000 tonnes expected to be delivered to one trading house alone.
Brent was rangebound, taking its cue from NYMEX crude.
March Brent was trading six cents up at $21.19 a barrel at 1816 GMT, having dipped to a low of $21.05 a barrel and touched a high at $21.38.
"We're basically tracking (NYMEX crude) which went through minor support and then bounced off the next one at $22.25," said one broker.
Brent breached light support at $21.20 a barrel as it came off highs and brokers said that the next support level was at $21.00 and Monday's low of $20.55.
Strong NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures were underpinning the whole complex, dealers said, but some expected Brent to test the downside again later in the session.
Dealers GNI said that the API data, set for release after the close of trade tonight, was not expected to throw up any big surprises.

"Crude looks moderately flat, gasoline should rise for seasonal reasons and distillates should draw down due to winter demand," GNI said in their daily report. "However, note the distillate draw at the same last year was quite dramatic so we're likely to see a larger surplus compared to year ago."
